title: How Face ID works in the dark

segments.text: How does Face ID work in the dark?
It covers your face in thousands of invisible dots.
Step one: infrared light. Your eyes can't see it, but your phone's infrared camera can, so it works even in total darkness.
Step two: a dot projector paints thousands of infrared dots onto your face.
The first Face ID iPhone used more than thirty thousand.
From those dots, your phone builds a 3D depth map of your face.
Step three: a protected part of the chip turns that map into numbers, and compares them with the face you set up.
That's why a photo can't unlock it: a photo has no depth.
And your face data never leaves your phone. Not even Apple can see it.

sources: https://support.apple.com/en-us/102381 (Apple, 'About Face ID advanced technology', read 2026-11-22): TrueDepth camera 'projecting and analyzing thousands of invisible dots to create a depth map of your face and also captures an infrared image'; a portion of the neural engine 'protected within the Secure Enclave' turns depth map + infrared image into 'a mathematical representation and compares that representation to the enrolled facial data'; 'designed to work indoors, outdoors, and even in total darkness'; 'Face ID always requires depth information, which isn't found in print or 2D digital photographs'; 'Face ID data doesn't leave your device, is never available to iOS or iPadOS, apps, or Apple'

https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2017/09/the-future-is-here-iphone-x/ (Apple Newsroom, iPhone X launch, 2017-09-12): TrueDepth camera 'made up of a dot projector, infrared camera and flood illuminator'; 'Face ID projects more than 30,000 invisible IR dots'
Note: Apple's current support article says 'thousands' of dots without a number; the 30,000+ figure is stated only for the first Face ID iPhone (iPhone X, 2017), and the script says exactly that.
